m_dialogEntries.m_dialog: This isn't politics, Sir. It's personal. The moment I met her, I knew she was the one, and nothing could keep us apart.
Geez, Freeder. Why are you acting like some kind of lovesick puppy dog? Stop being so serious. Get out and bask in the sun, why don't you?
The chairman has guests. If the Vice-Chair would be so kind as to excuse himself, we can move on to more pertinent business.
If you don't want me here, then I will indeed make myself scarce. But we will discuss this matter at a later time. I am resolved.
So... look what the Qhat dragged in. Finally we get the real negotiator from Aggrobah. This prissy little Djinni gets on my nerves.
It's Istar. My name? It's Istar.
Istar, Mistar, Whiskar... who cares? Look, you guys want an alliance, right? Maybe you do something for us, we do something for you.
Our Vassals - House Bumbai - are jealous, so they started this... rebellion. It's like they want to bring down the mountain for no reason!
It's infuriating. We Sayameez designed this Mountain. We allow the brutish Bumbai to stay, but only if they keep the cool air coming!
And that's what they'll do, because you, Wizard, you're going to make them. Go down to the Catsbah and meet Prefect Josapat. He knows what to do.
Is it me, Master, or were those Qhats really rude? Not that it matters, I suppose. For now, we just have to play along and find this Prefect.
Oh... ahem, I'm sorry. You must be the one sent by Chairman Meow to help with the Rebels. A sorry business, all this. Quite depressing, really.
I might've screwed things up with the House Djinni, Shamiss. I brought him this cute antique tea set, only to learn he hates antiques, and tea.
So, Shamiss is only willing to help so much, and of course, there's more - the real trouble here is that there's a rebellion under way.
It seems the Vassals here, House Bumbai, are rebelling against the Sayameez. Come with me up to the Basking Grounds and meet Chairman Meow.
The Chairman has an offer, some way we can get him to join the Aggrobah Alliance. It's a start, at least, isn't it, Master? Let's go.
